test_title: Most Repeated 2025 General Science PYQ Subject Test - 01
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT a property of ionic compounds?

options.text: They generally have high melting and boiling points.
They are generally solid at room temperature.
They can conduct electricity in an aqueous/molten state.
They are soluble in solvents such as kerosene and petrol.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They are soluble in solvents such as kerosene and petrol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Melting and Boiling Points**: Ionic compounds possess **high melting and boiling points**. This is due to the presence of a very strong **electrostatic force of attraction** between the **positively charged ions (cations)** and **negatively charged ions (anions)**, which requires a significant amount of **thermal energy** to overcome. ***Hence, statement 1 is a correct property.***
 
• **Physical Nature**: These compounds are **solids** and are somewhat **hard** at **room temperature** because of the strong force of attraction between the ions. They are generally **brittle** and tend to break into pieces when **pressure** is applied. ***Hence, statement 2 is a correct property.***
 
• **Electrical Conductivity**: The conduction of electricity through a solution involves the movement of **charged particles**. Ionic compounds **conduct electricity** in the **molten state** or when dissolved in **water (aqueous solution)** because the ions become free to move. However, they do **not conduct electricity** in the **solid state** because the movement of ions is restricted by the rigid **crystal structure**. ***Hence, statement 3 is a correct property.***
 
• **Solubility**: Electrovalent or ionic compounds are generally **soluble in water** (which is a **polar solvent**) but are **insoluble** in organic solvents such as **kerosene, petrol, benzene, and ether** (which are **non-polar solvents**). This follows the principle of **"like dissolves like."** ***Hence, statement 4 is NOT a property of ionic compounds.***
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Ionic Bonds**: An **ionic bond** is formed by the **complete transfer** of one or more **valence electrons** from a **metal atom** to a **non-metal atom**. This transfer results in the formation of **ions** that achieve a stable **noble gas electronic configuration**.
 
• **Lattice Energy**: The stability of an ionic compound is attributed to its **lattice energy**, which is the energy released when one mole of an ionic crystalline compound is formed from **gaseous ions**. **Magnesium Oxide (MgO)** and **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** are classic examples of such structures.
 
• **Crystal Lattice**: Ionic compounds do not exist as single molecules but as **aggregates** of ions arranged in a regular **three-dimensional** pattern called a **crystal lattice**. For instance, in **NaCl**, each **Sodium ion** is surrounded by six **Chloride ions** and vice-versa.
 
• **Comparison with Covalent Compounds**: Unlike ionic compounds, **covalent compounds** are formed by the **sharing of electrons**. They generally have **lower melting and boiling points**, can be **gases, liquids, or solids** at room temperature, and are typically **non-conductors** of electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dielectric Constant**: Water has a high **dielectric constant** (approx. **80**), which weakens the **electrostatic forces** between ions, facilitating their **dissociation** and making water an excellent solvent for ionic substances.
 
• **Hydration Energy**: When an ionic compound dissolves in water, the ions are surrounded by water molecules, a process called **hydration**. If the **hydration energy** is higher than the **lattice energy**, the compound will be **soluble**.
 
• **Chemical Reactivity**: Reactions involving ionic compounds in **aqueous solutions** are usually very **fast** because they occur between **free ions** rather than neutral atoms or molecules.
